description: Stars & Beyond is a multidisciplinary team bringing together different perspectives and skills to tackle challenges in space exploration. Combining technology, scientific research, data analysis, and creative problem-solving, we developed Atlas as our contribution to making complex scientific knowledge more accessible and useful.
summary:
We are Team Stars & Beyond, driven by the mission to make space exploration safer and democratize access to scientific knowledge about how fire behaves beyond Earth.
To achieve this, we developed Atlas Stars & Beyond (Extinction Atlas), an interactive scientific intelligence platform that consolidates decades of microgravity combustion research from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. Atlas maps documented experiments across oxygen concentrations, atmospheric pressures, and gravity regimes, connecting researchers, students, and engineers to critical experimental evidence with full file- and row-level traceability.
By making existing evidence accessible while explicitly revealing where experimental data is missing, Atlas accelerates the investigation of fire prevention and suppression strategies for future space missions.
details:
Atlas Stars & Beyond is a scientific intelligence and visualization platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Flame in Freefall). Its purpose is to transform decades of microgravity combustion research into accessible, interactive, and actionable engineering knowledge.

The platform addresses the challenge of fragmented aerospace fire safety data by bringing together experimental records, deterministic physical calculations, multidimensional data visualization, and a real-time WebGL2 3D combustion solver within a unified analytical environment.

By combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), deterministic evidence rules implemented in Go, interactive dataset exploration, and real-time 3D visualization, Atlas enables researchers and engineers to investigate hypotheses across different spacecraft habitats and materials. Users can adjust environmental parameters—including gravity regimes, atmospheric pressure, and oxygen concentration—to assess experimental coverage, compare fire suppression strategies (such as CO₂ and helium), and examine scientific evidence with full source traceability down to the original file and row.

Beyond retrieving existing literature, Atlas functions as a discovery engine for space fire safety. Through interactive 3D test maps, evidence knowledge graphs, flammability limit visualizations, and the Next Fire gap-analysis queue, the platform reveals underexplored physical conditions—such as partial gravity on the Moon and Mars—and identifies promising directions for future experiments.

By bridging historical NASA datasets with interactive simulation and evidence-grounded AI synthesis, Atlas accelerates scientific investigation and supports the development of safer fire prevention and suppression protocols for future long-duration space missions.

Repository Access – GitHub

Organization: https://github.com/stars-beyond

Backend & Data Pipelines: https://github.com/stars-beyond/atlas-fire-extintion-backend

Frontend & 3D Lab: https://github.com/stars-beyond/atlas-fire-extintion-front

The Problem

Over several decades, NASA has conducted thousands of experiments and published extensive research on fire behavior in microgravity environments, including 24 combustion investigations available through the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) system.

Despite the critical importance of this knowledge for crewed mission safety, the sheer volume of research—and its distribution across heterogeneous tables, PDFs, and technical reports—makes it difficult to retrieve, interpret, and compare experimental findings.

Researchers and engineers must spend considerable time searching and cross-referencing studies to understand how different materials, atmospheric compositions, and ventilation conditions influence combustion. This fragmentation also makes it harder to identify patterns, compare experimental outcomes, and recognize scientific gaps, limiting the ability of existing research to guide future investigations.

The Gap

Advances in artificial intelligence, data engineering, and real-time browser-based simulation create new opportunities to explore large scientific archives. However, a generic chatbot built on top of PDFs is not sufficient for aerospace fire safety: it cannot reliably guarantee source traceability, distinguish measured outcomes from extrapolations, or reveal where experimental evidence is simply unavailable.

For example, future lunar habitats are expected to operate at oxygen concentrations of 30% or higher and atmospheric pressures of 10.2 psi or lower. However, solid-material combustion tests in the NASA PSI archive were conducted at oxygen concentrations ranging from 13.6% to 22.2%, near 1 atm. Furthermore, PSI contains no combustion tests conducted under partial-gravity conditions representative of the Moon or Mars.

This reveals a critical gap between the availability of historical experimental data and the ability to analyze it systematically—making both existing evidence and missing experimental conditions immediately visible.

Our Solution

Atlas is an integrated platform that enables users to investigate, analyze, compare, and explore fire behavior across diverse space environments.

Its backend consolidates 24 NASA PSI combustion investigations, comprising 1,972 tabulated tests (1,153 of which include oxygen and pressure metadata), a hybrid PostgreSQL + pgvector search index, a deterministic evidence engine implemented in Go, and a RAG pipeline containing 18,436 indexed document chunks from NASA PSI and NTRS.

Rather than generating unsupported risk scores, Atlas computes a transparent, four-level Evidence Verdict for each scenario:

Measured: Experimental tests are available under the target atmospheric conditions (±2% O₂ and ±20% pressure) and gravity regime.

Bounded: No tests exist at the exact gravity level, but experimental data is available at both 0 g and 1 g under comparable atmospheric conditions, providing bounds for analysis.

One-sided: Experimental tests are available at only one of the two reference gravity levels (0 g or 1 g).

Terra Incognita: No NASA PSI experimental tests are available under the target atmospheric conditions.

When experimental evidence exists (Measured), Atlas reports empirical outcomes directly, such as the number of samples that burned completely, self-extinguished, or failed to ignite.

When experimental evidence is unavailable, the platform does not fabricate probabilities or unsupported conclusions. Instead, it clearly communicates the limits of existing knowledge: AI generates the explanation, while the underlying data determines the verdict.

How It Works

When users access Atlas, they can explore the platform through a guided configurator (Test Drive) or navigate directly to its analytical modules.

1. Habitat & Free-Text Inference

Users can select from six preset environments: Space Station, Lunar Base, Rover, Mars Habitat, Spacesuit, or Earth Room. Alternatively, they can manually adjust oxygen concentration, atmospheric pressure, and gravity.

A natural-language input—for example, "lunar rover with 34% oxygen and Nomex seats"—automatically extracts the relevant parameters and configures the Test Drive.

2. Material Selection

Users select a fuel family and material, including cotton fabric, acrylic/PMMA, Nomex, silicone, liquid fuels, or gases. For each selection, Atlas displays the exact number of NASA experiments available.

3. Test Drive & Interactive 3D Stage

Clicking Light activates the flame in the 3D environment and reveals the four-level Evidence Verdict.

Three tabs guide the investigation:

Evidence: Displays the verdict, empirical rates, and the closest matching NASA experiments. Selecting a test opens its exact source file, row, and original experimental record.

Extinguish: Allows users to release CO₂ or helium, reduce cabin ventilation, and examine FLEX droplet burn-rate regressions and extinction behavior.

Ask: Provides a natural-language scientific Q&A interface powered by RAG, featuring Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming, clickable numbered citations, rendered LaTeX equations, and source page references.

4. Multi-View Stage

The main visualization area seamlessly switches between multiple analytical environments:

3D Combustion Lab (lab3d): A real-time WebGL2 3D combustion visualization.

3D Test Map: Maps experimental coverage across gravity regimes, with each floor representing a different gravity condition and visibly exposing empty Moon and Mars floors.

Knowledge Graph: Connects the selected scenario to related experiments, revealing relationships between experimental conditions and available evidence.

Flammability Limits: Provides an interactive view of flammability boundaries.

Thermal Camera: An ONNX-powered prediction tool for PMMA film flame spread.

5. Technical Dossier, Dashboard & Mission Story

Atlas also provides tools for deeper scientific investigation and reporting:

Technical Dossier: Generates downloadable Markdown or printable reports containing relevant technical findings.

Scientific Intelligence Dashboard: Allows users to build custom scatter plots, bar charts, and histograms using 15 API datasets, with CSV/PNG export and row-level drill-down.

Investigation Comparison: Enables side-by-side analysis of different experimental investigations.

Next Fire: Presents a gap-analysis queue highlighting opportunities for future experiments.

Mission Story: Offers interactive 3D mission scenarios powered by precomputed trajectories from mission-fire-engine.

Implementation Details

DATA PIPELINES

  • Data ingestion and preparation are handled by modular Python pipelines (brain/atlas/ and ml/):
  • Sources (psi.py): Retrieves combustion investigations, catalogs, and experimental tables from NASA PSI, with local caching and an offline seed fallback (data/seed/).
  • Adapters (adapters.py): Uses table-specific normalization adapters to map heterogeneous experimental records into a unified schema while preserving original file names, line numbers, raw records, and explicit flags for inferred fields (such as assuming a cabin pressure of 1 atm for solid-material tests when the original value is not specified).
  • Documents & Embeddings (docs.py, rag-index): Extracts text from NASA PSI PDFs and challenge resources using PyMuPDF and pypdf. Atlas documents are embedded locally using fastembed, while the RAG collection (flame_freefall_2026_v6) indexes 18,436 chunks from NASA PSI and NTRS in PostgreSQL + pgvector using OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large.
  • ML & Thermal Models (ml/): Includes cross-validated linear regression for FLEX droplet burn rates, as well as scripts (spread_table.py, export_thermal.py) that export Atlas-MachineL neural models into lookup grids and ONNX networks for predicting PMMA film spread speed and surface temperature under 0 g conditions.

BACKEND

  • API (api/, Go 1.25): A domain-driven Go service covering evidence, catalog, flammability, prediction, Q&A, search, datasets, and simulation modules. Connected to PostgreSQL via pgx/v5, it computes all deterministic verdicts, investigation rankings, empirical burn rates, flammability assessments, knowledge graph topologies, dataset charts, and hybrid RRF search. It also proxies SSE-based Q&A streaming (/api/ask/stream) to the RAG service, with graceful fallback to Anthropic Claude, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or extractive mode when API keys are unavailable.
  • RAG Service (rag/, Python + FastAPI): Runs the team's rag-Carlin pipeline, adapted to PostgreSQL + pgvector (atlas_pg/), delivering evidence-grounded answers with numbered citations, reviewed equations, and conversation history.
  • Embedder Service (brain/, Python + FastAPI): Generates query embeddings through fastembed and executes ONNX-based thermal camera inference using onnxruntime.

FRONTEND

  • Stack: Built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, Recharts, react-markdown, remark-math, and rehype-katex. The architecture is organized by feature (configurator, stage, ask, findings, investigations, next-fire, dashboard, and story), with no scientific computations performed on the client side. Every verdict, ranking, and chart calculation is handled by the Go API.
  • 3D Combustion Lab (public/lab3d/): A real-time WebGL2 GPU combustion solver embedded through an iframe bridge (bridge.js) that receives physical constants and scenario parameters from /api/sim/config. The model is an uncalibrated study visualization, clearly labeled as such in the interface and kept strictly independent of the Evidence Verdict.
  • Deployment: Published as static assets on Cloudflare Workers & Pages (wrangler.jsonc), communicating with the Go API over HTTPS/CORS.

INFRASTRUCTURE

  • Containerization: Orchestrated through Docker and Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml), running the database (pgvector/pgvector:pg16), embedder, ingestion pipeline (with fingerprint-based atomic schema swapping from atlas_build to atlas), RAG indexing, RAG service, and API.
  • Production: Deployed behind Nginx and Cloudflare, with automated daily NASA PSI data refreshes through deploy/refresh.sh.

Impact

Atlas transforms complex, fragmented aerospace combustion research into accessible, traceable, and actionable engineering intelligence. By enabling researchers and engineers to compare experiments, visualize evidence coverage, identify knowledge gaps, and inspect original experimental records, the platform makes decades of NASA microgravity research more accessible and useful for future investigations.

Its scientific contribution goes beyond organizing existing data. Atlas helps reveal what current experiments can—and cannot—support, highlights underexplored conditions such as partial gravity and elevated-oxygen exploration atmospheres, and helps prioritize future experiments that could address the most significant knowledge gaps.

In practical terms, this means researchers can investigate scenarios more efficiently, identify where additional testing is needed, and make better-informed decisions when designing future experiments and fire suppression strategies.

The platform also has potential applications beyond aerospace research, including terrestrial environments such as enclosed battery rooms under 1 g conditions. By maintaining a clear distinction between experimental evidence, deterministic analysis, and exploratory simulation, Atlas supports evidence-based technical investigation without presenting itself as a flight-safety certification system.

Ultimately, Atlas helps turn fragmented scientific archives into a practical foundation for identifying risks, directing research efforts, and advancing fire safety in environments where reliable experimental knowledge is essential.

Conclusion

Atlas Stars & Beyond brings together deterministic engineering logic, multidimensional data visualization, real-time 3D simulation, and evidence-grounded AI to bridge the gap between historical microgravity combustion research and the challenges of future space exploration.

By making both experimental findings and their limitations visible, Atlas transforms how researchers access, interpret, and investigate scientific evidence. Its approach empowers a new generation of researchers and engineers to identify knowledge gaps, guide future experiments, and contribute to the development of safer habitats beyond Earth.
